records.name: Mariposa Food Co-op
records.summary: A member-owned grocery on Baltimore Avenue in West Philadelphia. Owners can take on an optional working member role that asks for at least four hours a month of store work.
records.what_you_do: Working members get training and staff help on their first few shifts, then help with store work. The program is being restarted, so ask the co-op what openings exist now.

schedule.text: Optional working member shifts, at least four hours a month. The page gives no fixed shift times.

cost.text: Ownership cost is not stated on the working member page

first_step.how: Become an owner, then email the co-op about the working member program
first_step.basis: The store is open to shoppers, but working shifts need membership and the program is being restarted, so the way in is unclear

records.notes: Older articles from 2009 and 2012 described required shifts; the current page says optional. The working member page carries an undated notice that the program is being brought back. Store hours were not on the pages read. Kind set to club as the closest fit for a member-owned co-op.

records.name: South Philly Food Co-op
records.summary: A member-owned grocery on South Juniper Street. Its online volunteer form lets people offer help with community events, marketing, event planning, handy jobs, and office work.
records.what_you_do: Pick the roles you want on the online volunteer form, such as tabling at community events, event planning, marketing, or admin support. The site does not say how many hours each role takes.

schedule.text: Volunteer hours and shift times are not listed on the site.

cost.text: Membership cost is not stated on the site; non-members can shop

first_step.how: Fill out the volunteer form on the co-op's website
first_step.basis: A public form takes a name, email and chosen roles; the site describes no training or screening

records.notes: Homepage banners name an October Equity Drive and an October 2026 event with no exact dates; that is the basis for the status. The volunteer page lists interest roles only. The bare domain has a TLS name mismatch, so the www address was used. The email address is obscured on the site, so only the phone is recorded. Any member work requirement is not stated on the site.

records.name: Vetri Community Partnership Teaching Kitchen
records.summary: A nonprofit teaching kitchen on Spring Garden Street that runs public cooking classes and nutrition education for people of all ages.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a public cooking class through the group's class schedule. The group also offers cooking classes and rents its space to community and corporate groups.

schedule.text: Public classes are listed on the group's class calendar. Days, times and dates could not be read from the pages available.

cost.text: Class cost is not shown on the pages that could be read

first_step.how: Register for a public class through the class schedule linked from the group's website
first_step.basis: The site says it welcomes people of all ages and links a sign-up page; the class details could not be read

records.notes: The group's own class and program pages returned HTTP 403, so class days, costs and volunteer roles are not recorded. The volunteer roles PDF carries a December 2024 date in its file metadata, but its text was not readable. Listed as a partner on Slow Food Philadelphia's volunteer page. A re-check from a browser would fill in the schedule.

records.name: Slow Food Philadelphia
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of the Slow Food movement. It holds member dinners and food education events, and it is run by volunteers.
records.what_you_do: Join as a member, come to chapter dinners, or volunteer. The volunteer page also lists partner food projects that need help, including an urban farm, a family cooking program, and a hoop house.

schedule.text: Chapter dinners and events. The next one listed is a banquet on Thursday, October 22, 2026 at 6 pm in Queen Village.

cost.text: The October 2026 banquet costs $30, with $5 going to the chapter. Membership dues are not stated.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to a public chapter event, or use the join page to become a member
first_step.basis: Events are posted publicly and the site has a join page, though no beginner program is described

records.notes: The homepage both lists the October 22, 2026 banquet and says no events are scheduled, so the specific event listing is the basis for the status. The banquet is BYOB and gluten free, and the organizers say they cannot accommodate allergies. Leaders and chapter history appeared only in search results and are not recorded.

records.name: The Food Trust: Farmers Market Volunteers
records.summary: The Food Trust runs farmers markets in Philadelphia. Volunteers help at a market each week or in the office supporting one of its programs.
records.what_you_do: Help at a farmers market each week, or help in the office with a program. The group takes separate interest forms for individuals and for groups.

schedule.text: Weekly help at a farmers market or program office. Shift lengths and hours are not listed.

locations.label: Philadelphia farmers markets and program office

cost.text: The cost of volunteering is not stated

first_step.how: Fill out the individual volunteer interest form on The Food Trust's site
first_step.basis: Open to individuals and groups through a public form; the site describes no beginner program

records.notes: The volunteer section names no specific markets and no shift times. A postponed Senior Appreciation Day at Clark Park Farmers Market was mentioned with no date. The June 2026 press release would not yield its text, so the status rests on the file's date and the volunteer page itself. A possible Friends of Headhouse volunteer group is kept as a lead, not a record.

records.name: Homebrewers of Philadelphia and Suburbs (HOPS)
records.summary: A homebrewing club for the Delaware Valley that meets monthly to share brewing know-how and has run homebrew competitions.
records.what_you_do: Members meet monthly, share brewing tips, and can post to the club's mailing list. The club has run homebrew competitions in past years.

schedule.text: Monthly meetings on the third Thursday, usually about 6 to 8 pm, at Home Sweet Homebrew or at area BYOB restaurants. Some meetings start earlier or run later.

cost.text: Dues are not listed on the club's page

first_step.how: Email the club contact named on its site for membership information
first_step.basis: The club names a contact and a monthly meeting, but the page is old and the steps to join are brief

records.notes: The newest dated item on the site is competition results from 2019, with no month shown, and the footer says the page was last updated in June 2014. Current meetings could not be confirmed. Meeting places have no published street address, so no location is recorded. The club serves Philadelphia and its suburbs; how many members are city residents is not stated. Dormant follows the rule for newest dated evidence.

records.name: The People's Kitchen
records.summary: A community kitchen at 1149 South 9th Street that cooks free meals for people in need and runs a community fridge. A 2023 news report described daily volunteer kitchen shifts.
records.what_you_do: A 2023 news report said kitchen volunteers unload deliveries, cook, and hand out meals beside a trained chef. The group's website lists office help, garden plot care, and special-event help for group and corporate volunteers.

schedule.text: A 2023 news report said meals were served from 10 to 11 am every day. The current meal schedule is not shown on the website.

first_step.how: Email the group or use the Get Involved page on its website
first_step.basis: A public volunteer page and email address; the site does not say whether volunteer openings exist now

records.notes: The newest dated item found is a January 2023 news report, so the status is dormant. The website's own posts are undated, and its newsletter sign-up showed a builder error. The 2023 report describes a partnership with South Philly Barbacoa and the 215 People's Alliance. The hunger family may also want this record, since it runs community meals.

records.name: Lutheran Settlement House Community Meal
records.summary: A monthly community dinner in Fishtown, open to anyone in the neighborhood, held at the Lutheran Settlement House office on Frankford Avenue.
records.what_you_do: Come to eat with neighbors. Staff and volunteers cook some meals, and local restaurants supply others. The listing does not describe volunteer roles for the meal.

schedule.text: Monthly, on the third Thursday, 5 to 6 pm, per the group's event listing

cost.text: The event page does not say whether the meal costs anything

first_step.how: Come to the Fishtown office on the third Thursday; the listing says anyone may attend
first_step.basis: The listing says it is open to anyone in the community, with no sign-up described

records.notes: The newest dated community meal found is April 20, 2023. The events page and homepage showed no 2025 or 2026 meal, so the monthly meal may have changed or stopped; a call to the office would confirm. One listed meal was sponsored by a city ward; only the settlement house program is recorded, not the sponsor. The office also runs a food pantry, which is not recorded here.

records.name: Supper (free community dinners)
records.summary: Free dinners open to anyone at four churches in Northwest Philadelphia. St. Martin-in-the-Fields began the program in 2012, and the four churches serve five dinners a month between them.
records.what_you_do: Help cook and serve, or share music or a talent with guests. Some churches also run a small activity table, such as arts and crafts or book giveaways.

schedule.text: Five dinners a month at four churches, per a 2019 article: St. Martin's on the second and fourth Wednesdays; Christ Church and St. Michael's on the fourth Saturday, 3 to 5 pm; St. Alban's on the second Tuesday; Grace Epiphany on the third Wednesday. Most run from 6 pm for about an hour.

locations.label: Christ Church and St. Michael's, Germantown

first_step.how: Go to one of the four churches on its dinner night
first_step.basis: Anyone may attend with no requirement to take part in religious activities, though the 2019 article describes no sign-up

records.notes: Only a May 2019 news article was read. The program's own website and any current dinners were not found in this session, so the status is dormant on the newest dated evidence. Confirm with the churches before treating it as current. Website and contacts are left empty because none was read.

leads_only.name: Greensgrow Farm
leads_only.note: Named on Slow Food Philadelphia's volunteer page as an urban farm that takes volunteers on a limited basis after an orientation. That page gives no link to the farm's own site, so the site was not checked and no domain was guessed. Urban farming, so the gardening family may want it.

leads_only.name: Friends of Headhouse Farmers Market (The Food Trust)
leads_only.note: A search summary described a June 2026 Food Trust press release announcing a volunteer group for the Headhouse market as coming soon. The PDF text would not load, so the launch is unconfirmed.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Homebrew Club (hosted by Philly Homebrew Outlet)
leads_only.note: A 2014 profile says the shop hosts this club on the third Friday of the month. The article returned HTTP 403 when fetched, and the shop's own website and the club's current status are not known.

notes: Searches: all 10 used, so the hard cap is reached. Fetches: 37, no rate limiting seen. Records: 9 written, all verdict publish; hide 0, not_a_group 0, duplicate 0, out_of_area 0. Dropped with reasons: (1) Sunday Suppers, a nine-month family cooking program. The domain sundaysuppersphilly.org now shows unrelated gambling content, and the only real evidence is an October 2016 article describing a program at Memphis Street Academy in Port Richmond. Not recorded; a re-check is worth doing. (2) Community Partnership School is a school, not a group. (3) Inquirer Food Fest (Nov 14, 2026) and The Great Chefs Event (Alex's Lemonade Stand) are one-off events. (4) Herman's Coffee and Market and City Winery are businesses with wine club tastings, not community groups. (5) Suburban homebrew clubs (Main Line Brewers Association, BUZZ in West Chester, Stoney Creek Homebrewers, Keystone Hops) are outside Philadelphia. Gaps: no search budget was spent on foodie meetups (Meetup and similar are leads only), Creekside Co-op (not found), or Clark Park market volunteer roles (none found). Heritage cooking: only the Oldways and Free Library series came up, and those pages were blocked. Supper's current status and LSH's current meal are unconfirmed. Kind choices: the two co-ops are set to club as the closest fit for member-owned groceries; community meals and the Food Trust volunteer program are set to program. Dormant records (HOPS, The People's Kitchen, Lutheran Settlement community meal, Supper) rest on newest dated items from 2019 or 2023 and each needs a call to confirm. Mariposa's working member page calls the program optional, while 2009 and 2012 articles described required shifts. Vetri's class and volunteer pages returned 403, so its schedule is not recorded.
